about: The server's character creation system: it owns every creation, respec, level-up and change-appearance session. The Osiris calls only append a request (the character's entity and a user id, 16 bytes) to one of its arrays; the bytes at +0x250 and +0x288 refuse new requests while set. The Toolkit exports its methods: RequestChangeAppearance, RequestRespec, RequestFullRespec, RequestUpdateChangeAppearance, RequestUpdateCreation, RequestOverrideAparenceVisual, RequestRemoveCustomVisualOvirride, RequestToggleAccessorySet, RequestAbort, Update.

evidence.says: the Toolkit's EoCServer.dll exports the class esv::character_creation::System with 44 methods, and the game's executable registers a system of that name (its index is taken as TypeIndex of esv::character_creation::System in the systems context)

the handlers of StartRespec (bg3_dx11.exe+0x36ACE20) and StartChangeAppearance (bg3_dx11.exe+0x36AD7A0) test +0x250 and +0x288 and append to the arrays at +0x438 (count +0x444, capacity +0x440) and +0x4E8 (count +0x4F4, capacity +0x4F0)

questions.ask: the field names are ours; read the Toolkit's RequestRespec and RequestChangeAppearance for the members they write, and find the readers of the two arrays in Update; what sets +0x250 and +0x288 (most likely a creation in progress and an unloading session)
